questions.question: What is Amazon Bedrock?

options.text: A managed EC2 instance type for AI workloads
A fully managed service for accessing foundation models via API
A machine learning training platform where you train your own models
An AWS storage service for AI datasets

explanation.correct: Amazon Bedrock provides API access to pre-trained foundation models from multiple providers — you don't manage any model infrastructure.
explanation.why: A describes EC2, C describes SageMaker training, D describes S3.

questions.question: Which AWS region must be used for this GenAI bot exercise?

options.text: us-east-1 (N. Virginia)
eu-west-1 (Ireland)
us-west-2 (Oregon)
ap-southeast-1 (Singapore)

explanation.correct: The exercise is designed for us-west-2 (Oregon) because not all Bedrock features are available in every region.
explanation.why: Other regions may lack the specific Bedrock features or model access needed for the lab.

questions.question: Why does the EC2 instance need an IAM role to call Amazon Bedrock?

options.text: EC2 instances always require an IAM role regardless of what they do
The IAM role provides the EC2 instance with temporary credentials to call Bedrock securely without hardcoding keys
Amazon Bedrock requires IAM roles as a billing mechanism
IAM roles encrypt the data sent to Bedrock

explanation.correct: IAM roles give EC2 temporary, auto-rotating credentials via the Instance Metadata Service. Boto3 picks these up automatically — no hardcoded keys needed.
explanation.why: Hardcoding long-term access keys in code is a security risk. IAM roles solve this cleanly.

questions.question: What is Boto3?

options.text: A Python web framework for building REST APIs
The AWS SDK for Python, named after an Amazonian river dolphin
A Bedrock-specific library only used for AI calls
A database connector for DynamoDB

explanation.correct: Boto3 is the AWS SDK for Python. It is named after the boto, a pink freshwater dolphin that lives in the Amazon River.
explanation.why: Boto3 can be used to call any AWS service — S3, DynamoDB, EC2, Bedrock, and more. It is not limited to AI calls.

questions.question: What does sudo chmod +x /var/www/cgi-bin/process_text.py do?

options.text: Makes the Python file readable by all users
Changes ownership of the file to Apache
Makes the Python file executable so Apache can run it as a CGI script
Encrypts the Python file for security

explanation.correct: chmod +x adds the execute bit to the file's permissions, allowing the OS (and Apache) to run it as an executable program.
explanation.why: Without the execute bit, Apache returns an Internal Server Error when trying to run the CGI script.

questions.question: What is a daemon in the context of this session?

options.text: A malicious background process
A background process that waits for requests and responds when called
A scheduled batch job in Linux
The root user account on a Linux system

explanation.correct: A daemon is a background process (like Apache httpd) that runs silently until it receives a request, then springs into action to handle it.
explanation.why: The term comes from Unix. Apache (httpd) is a daemon — it sits waiting until a browser sends an HTTP request.

questions.question: What IAM policy is attached to the EC2 role in this exercise?

options.text: AmazonEC2FullAccess
AdministratorAccess
AmazonBedrockFullAccess
AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess

explanation.correct: AmazonBedrockFullAccess is attached to give the EC2 instance permission to call any Bedrock API, including InvokeModel.
explanation.why: Todd noted this is wider than needed for production — in real environments, you'd narrow to specific actions and model ARNs.

questions.question: What command starts and enables Apache to run on boot?

options.text: sudo apache2 start && sudo apache2 enable
sudo systemctl start httpd && sudo systemctl enable httpd
sudo yum start httpd && sudo yum enable httpd
sudo httpd --start && sudo httpd --enable

explanation.correct: systemctl is the Linux service manager. 'start' runs the service now; 'enable' configures it to start automatically on every reboot.
explanation.why: The service is named 'httpd' (HTTP daemon) — the Apache package on Amazon Linux.

questions.question: Why does the simple bot not remember previous messages?

options.text: Amazon Bedrock doesn't support conversation history
The Python CGI script runs fresh on each request with no persistent state
Claude models don't support multi-turn conversations
The HTML form doesn't include a session ID

explanation.correct: Each HTTP request triggers a new CGI process execution. The script has no memory between runs — no state is stored anywhere.
explanation.why: Memory requires something external (file, database) to persist between executions. The simple bot has none of this.

questions.question: What does temperature=0.9 control in a Bedrock API call?

options.text: The processing speed of the model
The maximum length of the response
The creativity and randomness of the model's output (higher = more creative)
The number of tokens the model considers at each step

explanation.correct: Temperature controls output randomness/creativity. 0 produces deterministic, focused responses. 1.0 produces maximum creativity and variability.
explanation.why: max_tokens controls length. top_k controls token candidate pool size. Temperature specifically controls entropy of the distribution.

questions.question: What is an Inference Profile in Amazon Bedrock?

options.text: A user profile that controls who can access Bedrock models
A configuration that routes requests across multiple regions for higher availability and throughput
A billing profile that tracks Bedrock costs per user
A model fine-tuning configuration

explanation.correct: Inference Profiles route API requests across multiple AWS regions, providing better availability and throughput than single-region endpoints.
explanation.why: From a code perspective, you use a profile ID the same way as a model ID — the routing is transparent.

questions.question: What is the hard timeout limit for API Gateway that can cause issues with multi-invocation AI workflows?

options.text: 10 seconds
29 seconds
60 seconds
5 minutes

explanation.correct: API Gateway has a hard, immutable 29-second timeout that cannot be changed. When multiple sequential model invocations exceed this, the request fails.
explanation.why: Todd's enhanced bot switched to Lambda Function URLs to avoid this limit, as Function URLs support longer execution times.

questions.question: What does 'sudo' do in Linux commands like 'sudo yum install httpd'?

options.text: Downloads the package from a secure (sudo = secure download) server
Runs the command with superuser/root privileges
Creates a secure tunnel before running the command
Verifies the package signature before installing

explanation.correct: sudo (superuser do) temporarily elevates your privileges to root for that one command. It is the Linux way of escalating permissions without logging in as root.
explanation.why: Todd logs in as ec2-user (less privileged) and uses sudo only when needed — a security best practice to reduce blast radius of mistakes.

questions.question: In the Python script, what does boto3.client('bedrock-runtime', region_name='us-west-2') do?

options.text: Installs the Bedrock SDK into the script
Creates an authenticated Bedrock client that uses the EC2 instance's IAM role credentials
Opens a direct network socket to Amazon Bedrock
Logs into the Bedrock console programmatically

explanation.correct: boto3.client() creates a service client pre-configured with credentials from the EC2 instance's IAM role (retrieved via Instance Metadata Service) and the specified region.
explanation.why: No access keys are passed — Boto3 automatically discovers credentials from the IAM role attached to the instance.

questions.question: What is RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation)?

options.text: A technique for retraining foundation models with new data
A pattern that retrieves relevant documents at query time and adds them to the prompt before model generation
An AWS service for generating synthetic training data
A method for compressing model parameters to reduce cost

explanation.correct: RAG retrieves relevant information from a knowledge store and injects it into the prompt, giving the model access to current or private information without requiring retraining.
explanation.why: Fine-tuning (A) modifies the model itself. RAG augments individual queries at runtime — faster, cheaper, and easier to keep current.

questions.question: What is the purpose of sudo chmod 755 /var/www/cgi-bin?

options.text: Makes all Python files in cgi-bin executable
Gives the directory read and execute access so Apache can list and invoke CGI scripts in it
Encrypts the cgi-bin directory
Removes write access from all users to prevent tampering

explanation.correct: 755 = owner has rwx, group has r-x, others have r-x. Apache (running as a different user) needs read + execute on the directory to access and run scripts inside it.
explanation.why: Without this, Apache cannot traverse into cgi-bin even if individual files are executable.

questions.question: What does the 'Content-Type: text/html' print statement at the top of the Python CGI script do?

options.text: Configures Apache to treat the file as an HTML template
Sends the required HTTP response header that tells the browser what type of content follows
Converts the Python output to HTML automatically
Enables the cgitb error tracer for HTML output

explanation.correct: CGI requires the script to output HTTP headers before any content. The Content-Type header tells the browser how to interpret the body that follows.
explanation.why: Without this header, the browser may display raw text instead of rendering HTML, or return a server error.

questions.question: Why is the context window limit important when building a bot with memory?

options.text: It limits how many users can access the bot simultaneously
The model cannot process more text than fits in the context window — including history, instructions, retrieved docs, and the current message
It determines the maximum cost per API call
It sets the maximum file size for knowledge base documents

explanation.correct: The context window is the total token budget for a single API call. As conversation history grows, it eventually consumes the entire budget, causing errors.
explanation.why: Todd hit errors around 800KB of history (~120,000 words). Solutions include summarization, sliding window, or storing history in a database.

questions.question: How does the enhanced bot solve the problem of outdated model knowledge?

options.text: It retrains the Claude model weekly with new data
It uses a Bedrock Knowledge Base (RAG) to retrieve current documents and inject them into the prompt
It scrapes Wikipedia on every request
It uses the top_p parameter to access more recent training data

explanation.correct: The enhanced bot queries a Bedrock Knowledge Base before calling Claude. Relevant documents are retrieved and appended to the user's prompt, grounding the model in current information.
explanation.why: RAG is the standard pattern for this. Retraining (A) is expensive and slow. top_p (D) has nothing to do with knowledge currency.

questions.question: What happens to conversation state when the Python CGI script finishes executing?

options.text: State is automatically saved to a session cookie in the browser
State is cached in Apache's memory for the next request
State is lost — the Python process exits and all in-memory data disappears
State is saved to the EC2 instance's swap space

explanation.correct: CGI processes are stateless — each request spawns a new process that lives only for the duration of that request. Memory is gone when the process exits.
explanation.why: This is why external persistence (file, database) is required for memory. The process lifecycle is request-scoped.

questions.question: A team is building a customer support bot using Amazon Bedrock. The bot needs access to internal product documentation that is updated weekly. Which approach best addresses this requirement?

options.text: Fine-tune the Claude model with the documentation every week
Embed the documentation text into the system prompt on every request
Use Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with the documentation in S3, and use RAG to retrieve relevant sections per query
Pre-generate all possible answers and store them in DynamoDB

explanation.correct: Bedrock Knowledge Bases with S3-backed RAG handles this perfectly. Update the S3 documents weekly, and the retrieval system automatically uses the latest content. No model retraining required.
explanation.why: Fine-tuning (A) is expensive and slow for weekly updates. Embedding full docs in system prompt (B) may exceed context windows. Pre-generating answers (D) cannot handle unpredictable questions.

questions.question: An EC2-hosted GenAI bot works in the dev account but fails with AccessDeniedException on Bedrock calls in production. The code is identical. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The production EC2 instance is in a different Availability Zone
The production EC2 instance does not have an IAM role with Bedrock permissions attached
Amazon Bedrock is not available in the production region
The Python version differs between dev and production

explanation.correct: AccessDeniedException on AWS API calls almost always means the calling entity lacks the required IAM permissions. The most common cause in this scenario is a missing or misconfigured IAM role on the production instance.
explanation.why: AZ (A) is irrelevant to IAM. Python version (D) would cause a different error. Regional availability (C) would cause an endpoint error, not AccessDeniedException.

questions.question: You are building an enhanced bot that calls Bedrock three times per request (KB retrieval, text generation, image generation). Each call takes about 8 seconds. Which architecture component creates a hard failure at scale?

options.text: EC2 instance type t3.micro — too small for three API calls
API Gateway — its immutable 29-second timeout means three sequential 8-second calls (24s) pass but any latency increase causes failure
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases — limited to one query per session
Boto3 — has a built-in 20-second timeout for all API calls

explanation.correct: Three calls at 8 seconds = 24 seconds total, which is under 29 seconds but with zero margin. Any latency spike (network, model, KB retrieval) will exceed the hard 29-second API Gateway limit and fail.
explanation.why: Todd encountered this exact problem and solved it by switching to Lambda Function URLs. Instance type (A) does not affect API timeout. Boto3 (D) has configurable timeouts, not a hard 20s limit.

questions.question: What is the security implication of allowing SSH from 0.0.0.0/0 in the EC2 security group?

options.text: No implication — SSH is always encrypted and safe from any source
Any IP address on the internet can attempt to authenticate to the instance via SSH, increasing exposure to brute force attacks
The instance will automatically accept any SSH connection without authentication
AWS will block the instance after 24 hours for policy violation

explanation.correct: Allowing SSH from 0.0.0.0/0 exposes port 22 to the entire internet, making the instance a target for automated scanning and brute force login attempts.
explanation.why: Best practice: restrict SSH source to specific administrator IPs or use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to eliminate the need for inbound SSH entirely.

questions.question: A Lambda-based version of the bot needs to persist conversation history. Which storage solution best replaces the text file approach used on EC2?

options.text: Lambda's /tmp directory — it persists between invocations indefinitely
Environment variables — large enough for most conversation histories
Amazon DynamoDB — a managed NoSQL database accessible from Lambda with no persistent filesystem required
Amazon RDS MySQL — standard relational storage for Lambda

explanation.correct: DynamoDB is the natural choice for Lambda-based state. It's serverless, scales automatically, has low-latency reads, and is easily keyed by user/session ID. Todd's production tool uses this approach.
explanation.why: Lambda's /tmp (A) is ephemeral and cleared between cold starts. Environment variables (B) are too small and not per-session. RDS (D) requires VPC configuration and connection management.

questions.question: The Python script calls json.loads(response['body'].read()). What does this do?

options.text: Converts the response to a Python dictionary by parsing the JSON body returned by Bedrock
Saves the response to a JSON file on the EC2 instance
Sends a confirmation receipt back to Bedrock
Decrypts the encrypted response from Bedrock

explanation.correct: Bedrock's invoke_model returns a streaming body object. .read() gets the raw bytes, and json.loads() parses the JSON-formatted response into a Python dictionary that you can access with keys like ['content'].
explanation.why: Bedrock responses are always JSON. Without parsing, you have raw bytes, not usable Python data structures.

questions.question: What is the Shared Responsibility Model implication of running sudo yum update -y at the start of the lab?

options.text: AWS is responsible for all updates; running this command is unnecessary
AWS keeps the AMI current until you launch it; after launch, patching the OS is the customer's responsibility
The customer is responsible for all updates including the hypervisor
AWS automatically updates EC2 instances daily, so manual updates create conflicts

explanation.correct: Under the Shared Responsibility Model, AWS maintains the hypervisor and physical infrastructure plus the base AMI up to the moment of launch. Once you launch, keeping the OS patched is your responsibility as the customer.
explanation.why: Todd explicitly made this point in the session. Running yum update ensures you have security patches released after the AMI was created.

questions.question: What is top_k=250 controlling in the Bedrock API call?

options.text: The number of previous conversation turns the model can consider
The number of results returned from the Bedrock Knowledge Base
The number of top candidate tokens the model considers when predicting each next word
The maximum number of API calls per second

explanation.correct: top_k limits the pool of tokens the model considers at each prediction step to the k most likely tokens. A higher top_k allows more diversity; a lower top_k makes the model more focused.
explanation.why: top_p is a related parameter that works on cumulative probability instead. Both control the entropy of generation.

questions.question: Which two AWS services does Boto3 bridge in the simple GenAI bot?

options.text: Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB
EC2 (Python runtime) and Amazon Bedrock (Claude model)
IAM and Amazon CloudWatch
Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda

explanation.correct: Boto3 runs inside the Python script on EC2 and makes authenticated API calls to Amazon Bedrock's bedrock-runtime service, bridging the compute layer and the AI model layer.
explanation.why: The IAM role provides the permissions. Boto3 is the mechanism that actually makes the call. The bridge is EC2 ↔ Bedrock.

questions.question: Why does Todd prefer EC2 Instance Connect over traditional SSH with a key pair for this lab?

options.text: EC2 Instance Connect is faster than SSH
EC2 Instance Connect generates temporary short-lived SSH keys, eliminating key file management while still being browser-accessible
EC2 Instance Connect provides higher security than key-pair SSH
Key pairs are not supported on Amazon Linux 2023

explanation.correct: EC2 Instance Connect generates a temporary key pair valid for 60 seconds and injects it into the instance. No .pem file to store, lose, or manage. It's browser-accessible from the AWS Console.
explanation.why: Todd noted this is not recommended best practice for production (key pairs are safer for controlled access) but is much simpler for labs and demos.
